title: Best home loan rates
body:
O.P.
Interested to know what are some of the best home loan rates going around at the moment and more importantly how does one go about securing one......what is required eg. 20% deposit or more, $500K+ loan amount, loan type/duration, first home or investment etc?

---- replies ----
[User #1047852446 postsKeeleTTL: Hopefully > 85 yearsWhirlpool Forums Addict] I tend to find https://www.finder.com.au/home-loans a pretty good starting point.
If you have a funky credit history – you could also start with a broker like Naritas who are pretty good. Often they have cash back specials on top of the lender rates.
[User #3623923116 postsspl456Whirlpool Forums Addict] HSBC – 3.55% (3.57% comp rate)
https://www.hsbc.com.au/1/2/ thedifference?WT.ac=AUH_hlhvhp0916
50k min Redraw OO Only
[User #6008835791 postsgreenhawkQuips Are For The InsecureWhirlpool Forums Addict] Transformations writes...
what is required eg. 20% deposit or more, $500K+ loan amount, loan type/duration, first home or investment etc?
Generally you are at a better point to negotiate if you are
<80% LVR >$300K loan PPOR/OO redraw (no offset). paying P&I (Principle and Interest).
and on some banks, having a borrowing power limit that is a good bit higher than the loan amount. (ie: you are not borrowing to the hilt).
Not sure on the duration part of things, but I would think 20+ years would be better than < 10 years.
[User #498255239 postsTransformationsForum Regular] O.P.
Great thanks. Do people generally negotiate better rates with banks directly, either in person or over the phone instead of going via broker?
Getting 3.8-3.9% rate seems like well below most advertised rates yet I see people often quoting those after negotiating with the banks directly.
[User #9486515751 postsP10PXLWhirlpool Forums Addict] I'm going ahead with Reduce at 3.35% ...
http://www.reduceloans.com.a u/variable-home-loans/rate-b uster-standard-variable-home-loan/
[User #9486515751 postsP10PXLWhirlpool Forums Addict] Keele writes...
you could also start with a broker like Naritas who are pretty good. Often they have cash back specials on top of the lender rates.
Naritas Mates Rates Peach
all give cashback in different forms, but they dont always offer the cheapest lenders.
[User #6152863927 postsJamie.M Brokerwww.passgo.com.auWhirlpool Forums Addict] Whoever you go with – just ensure that the cheap rates isn't a honeymoon promo.
Just refinanced a client from an online cheapy mentioned above. They provided a low variable rate that was only applicable for one year – client was under the impression it wasn't a honeymoon rate so was surprised when it jumped up more than 1% a year later!
Discharge fees were massive too – and they're making it VERY hard to refinance away due to their clunky admin processes.
Cheers
Jamie

I'm going ahead with Reduce at 3.35% ...
I couldn't find anywhere mention of an offset? Nice rate though.
I'm still with loans.com.au who I've been with for 1.25 years, currently at 3.68%.

I'm going ahead with Reduce at 3.35% ...
http://www.reduceloans.com. au/variable-home-loans/rate- buster-standard-variable-home-loan/
Hey Matt Can you let us know how this process goes? I haven't heard of anyone actually going with them yet.
I did look at them, but l think some of their fees were a bit high and they aren't guaranteed by the Gov if something goes pear shaped.
[User #4876622068 postscroupWhirlpool Forums Addict] spl456 writes...
they aren't guaranteed by the Gov if something goes pear shaped.
Correct me if I'm wrong. But if a mortgage lender goes pear-shaped how does that negatively affect the borrower? Since they don't appear to offer an offset, there's no consequences, right?
IMO these online 'cheapies' are probably safer, as they require a leverage of <80% to even consider a mortgage application. It's all the other lenders who will take anyone and accept LMI who you should be more worried about.
[User #9486515751 postsP10PXLWhirlpool Forums Addict] this post was edited
spl456 writes...
Hey Matt Can you let us know how this process goes? I haven't heard of anyone actually going with them yet.
really good so far. the forms were a little confusing and took a few hours to complete. super quick email responses. conditionally approved in a few days subject to a few extra docs which I missed. full approval should be about a week or so. all pretty simple.
yes, the exit is $795 not $300 but with an interest rate difference of 3.35% vs my current 4.22%, it wont take long to get ahead.
I did look at them, but l think some of their fees were a bit high and they aren't guaranteed by the Gov if something goes pear shaped.
they are lending me money but have the security of my house.
if they try to steal my house and we go to court, I just need to demonstrate that I have been paying my mortgage payments and then the judge will not decide to let them steal & sell my house.
in simple terms, there's no risk.
i am not using any of their savings account as I will continue banking with BankWest.
Just a simple home loan which I'll dump the repayments into every fortnight.
[User #9486515751 postsP10PXLWhirlpool Forums Addict] croup writes...
Correct me if I'm wrong. But if a mortgage lender goes pear-shaped how does that negatively affect the borrower? Since they don't appear to offer an offset, there's no consequences, right?
correct. there is no risk from that perspective.
with offset is 3.44%: http://www.reduceloans .com.au/variable-home-loans/ rate-buster-offset-variable/
or 3.35% without.
I just went without offset as I only expect to only have about $5-10K in my transaction account and I can earn 1.5% interest on that plus I save mortage rate at 3.35% .. bit easier that way.
[User #4876622068 postscroupWhirlpool Forums Addict] matt-12 writes...
I just went without offset as I only expect to only have about $5-10K in my transaction account and I can earn 1.5% interest on that plus I save mortage rate at 3.35% .. bit easier that way.
You earn 1.5% on savings, for which you'd also pay income tax. Whereas, offset provides a full interest saving of 3.44% (with an offset account).
Doing a quick calculation for a $490,000 mortgage at 3.44% ($500k minus $10k offset) vs. $500,000 mortgage at 3.35%, you'd still be better off with the offset.
[User #9486515751 postsP10PXLWhirlpool Forums Addict] croup writes...
Doing a quick calculation for a $490,000 mortgage at 3.44% ($500k minus $10k offset) vs. $500,000 mortgage at 3.35%, you'd still be better off with the offset.
hmm .. maybe I should have checked properly .. but anyway .. i wanted the convenience of keeping as much as possible with BankWest (credit card, transaction acct, business acct).
[User #9486515751 postsP10PXLWhirlpool Forums Addict] loan approved with reduce.
summary: – fill out forms – 1 week conditional approval (conditional due to my payslip mixup) – 1 week for final approval (after submitting the correct payslips) Next steps: – loan contract about a week away for us to sign & return – settlement about to be booked after that in a week or so
